question: Norman Pritchard, India's sole representative at the 1900 Paris Olympics, won silver medals in which two events, making him India's first Olympic medal winner?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 200m sprint and 200m hurdles.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the 1900 Paris Olympics, Norman Pritchard was India's single representative, and won silver medals in both the 200m sprint and the 200m hurdles, making him India's first Olympic medal winner.

 

• This was also India's first Olympic participation at any level.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's first team-level Olympic participation came later, at the 1920 Antwerp Olympics (Belgium), marking the transition from individual to organised national team representation.

 

NOTE

 

• 100m/long jump, 400m/800m, and high jump/javelin (Options 1, 3, 4) are not the events in which Pritchard won his medals; his specific events were the 200m sprint and 200m hurdles.

question: India won its first Olympic gold medal at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics, in which sport, also becoming the first gold medal won by any Asian nation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hockey.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India won its first Olympic gold medal at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics, in Hockeyব— also marking the first gold medal won by any Asian nation at the Olympics.

 

• The hockey team's captain and vice-captain were Jai Pal Singh Munda and Broome Pinniger; Major Dhyan Chand scored the highest 14 goals in the tournament (across 5 matches).

 

• This began India's legendary hockey streak: 8 total hockey medals, including a consecutive streak of 6 golds (1928, 1932, 1936, 1948, 1952, 1956), plus further golds in 1964 (Tokyo) and 1980 (Moscow).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hockey was first played at the Olympics in 1908 (London), but India's dominance began specifically from the 1928 Amsterdam Games onward, launching one of the most remarkable winning streaks in Olympic history.

 

NOTE

 

• Wrestling, Shooting and Athletics (Options 1, 3, 4) are sports in which India later won individual medals, but India's historic first Olympic gold (1928) and first-ever-by-an-Asian-nation gold was specifically in Hockey.

question: At the 1952 Helsinki Olympics, which Indian wrestler became independent India's first individual Olympic medal winner?
option_4: Khashaba Dadasaheb Jadhav's contemporary, Rajyavardhan Rathore
solution_text:
The correct answer is K.D. Jadhav.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• K.D. Jadhav (wrestler) was the first individual medal winner of independent India, at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics, winning a Bronze medal in Wrestling.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• At the same 1952 Helsinki Olympics, Milkha Singh was not yet an Olympic medallist — his famous near-miss (finishing fourth in the 400m) occurred later, at the 1960 Rome Olympics.

 

NOTE

 

• Milkha Singh, Sushil Kumar and Rajyavardhan Rathore (Options 1, 3, 4) are all significant Indian Olympians, but K.D. Jadhav specifically holds the distinction of being independent India's first individual Olympic medallist (1952).

question: Milkha Singh, 'The Flying Sikh', famously finished fourth in the men's 400m final at the 1960 Rome Olympics, missing the bronze medal by how narrow a margin?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 0.1 second.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Milkha Singh set an Indian record by finishing fourth in the men's 400m at the 1960 Rome Olympics, with a timing of 45.6 seconds, missing the bronze medal by just 0.1 second.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• A similar heartbreakingly narrow miss occurred later with P.T. Usha, who finished fourth in the 400m hurdles final at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics, missing bronze by just 1/100th of a second.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 second, 0.01 second and 2 seconds (Options 1, 3, 4) do not match the documented margin; Milkha Singh's specific, famous near-miss was by 0.1 second.

question: P.T. Usha, also known as the 'Payyoli Express', achieved which historic distinction at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics?
option_1: She won India's first Olympic gold in athletics
option_2: She became the first female to reach the final of an Olympic athletics event, finishing fourth in the 400m hurdles
option_3: She became the first Indian woman to win an individual Olympic medal
option_4: She won a bronze medal in badminton
solution_text:
The correct answer is She became the first female to reach the final of an Olympic athletics event, finishing fourth in the 400m hurdles.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• P.T. Usha ('Payyoli Express') secured the fourth position in the final of the 400m hurdles at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics, missing the bronze medal by only 1/100th of a second.

 

• She was the first female to reach the final of an Olympic athletics event for India, a landmark achievement even without a medal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first Indian woman to actually win an individual Olympic medal was Karnam Malleswari, at the 2000 Sydney Olympics, in weightlifting — a distinction separate from Usha's earlier historic 'first female finalist' achievement.

 

NOTE

 

• Winning gold in athletics, winning an individual medal, and a badminton bronze (Options 1, 3, 4) describe achievements of Neeraj Chopra, Karnam Malleswari, and Saina Nehwal/P.V. Sindhu respectively, not P.T. Usha's specific 1984 achievement.

question: At the 2000 Sydney Olympics, Karnam Malleswari won a Bronze medal in weightlifting (69kg), achieving which historic first for India?
option_1: First Indian to win an Olympic gold medal
option_2: First Indian woman to win an individual Olympic medal
option_3: First Indian to compete in the Olympics
option_4: First Indian to win two Olympic medals
solution_text:
The correct answer is First Indian woman to win an individual Olympic medal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Karnam Malleswari won India's first medal (Bronze) in weightlifting (69kg) at the 2000 Sydney Olympics, and became the first Indian woman to win an individual Olympic medal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• This achievement predated by 16 years the moment when Saina Nehwal (2012, Badminton) and Mary Kom (2012, Boxing) became the first Indian women to win Olympic medals in their respective individual sports, and by 12 years the first time two Indian women won medals in the same Olympics (2012 London).

 

NOTE

 

• First Olympic gold, first Indian to compete, and first to win two medals (Options 1, 3, 4) describe other athletes/milestones (Abhinav Bindra, Norman Pritchard, and Sushil Kumar respectively), not Karnam Malleswari's specific 'first Indian woman' distinction.

question: At the 2008 Beijing Olympics, Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual gold medal in which event?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10m Air Rifle.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual gold medal at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, in the 10m Air Rifle shooting event.

 

• At the same 2008 Games, Vijender Singh won India's first Olympic boxing medal (Bronze), defeating Ecuador's Carlos Gongora, and was later honoured with the Padma Shri in 2010; Sushil Kumar won a Bronze medal in wrestling.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Abhinav Bindra's gold remained India's only individual Olympic gold medal for 13 years, until Neeraj Chopra won gold in Javelin Throw at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, becoming only the second Indian to achieve this feat.

 

NOTE

 

• 10m Air Pistol, Javelin Throw and 50m Rifle 3 Positions (Options 1, 3, 4) are events associated with other Indian shooters/athletes (Manu Bhaker, Neeraj Chopra, and Swapnil Kusale respectively), not Abhinav Bindra's specific gold-winning event.

question: At the 2012 London Olympics, India won a total of 6 medals (2 Silver, 4 Bronze) — double the tally from the 2008 Beijing Olympics. Which two Indian women won Olympic medals for the first time at these Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Saina Nehwal and Mary Kom.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the 2012 London Olympics, for the first time, Indian female athletes won two Olympic medals in the same edition: Saina Nehwal won Bronze in Badminton (the first Indian to win an Olympic medal in badminton), and Mary Kom won Bronze in Boxing (the first Indian boxer, male or female, to win an Olympic medal).

 

• Other 2012 medallists included Gagan Narang (Bronze, Shooting), Yogeshwar Dutt (Bronze, Wrestling), Vijay Kumar (Silver, 25m Rapid Fire Pistol), and Sushil Kumar (Silver, Wrestling — becoming the first Indian to win two Olympic medals, having also won Bronze in 2008).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sakshi Malik later became the first Indian woman wrestler to win an Olympic medal, at the 2016 Rio Olympics, a distinct milestone from Saina Nehwal and Mary Kom's 2012 achievements.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnam Malleswari/P.T. Usha, Mirabai Chanu/P.V. Sindhu, and Sakshi Malik/Deepa Malik (Options 1, 3, 4) are all significant Indian sportswomen, but the specific pair who first achieved dual female Olympic medals in 2012 London is Saina Nehwal and Mary Kom.

question: At the 2016 Rio Olympics, P.V. Sindhu achieved which historic first for India in badminton?
option_1: First Indian to win a badminton World Championship
option_2: First Indian player to win a silver medal in the history of the Olympics
option_3: First Indian woman to win an Olympic gold medal
option_4: First Indian to compete in Olympic badminton
solution_text:
The correct answer is First Indian player to win a silver medal in the history of the Olympics.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the 2016 Rio Olympics, P.V. Sindhu became the first Indian player to win a silver medal in the history of the Olympics (in Badminton).

 

• At the same Games, Sakshi Malik became the first woman wrestler to win an Olympic medal, and Aditi Ashoka represented India in golf on its Olympic debut (making the sport's first appearance since 1904).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• P.V. Sindhu went on to win a second Olympic medal (Bronze) at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, making her the first Indian woman to win two individual Olympic medals.

 

NOTE

 

• World Championship win, first female gold, and first Olympic badminton appearance (Options 1, 3, 4) are not the specific documented 'first' for Sindhu at Rio 2016; her landmark achievement there was being the first Indian to win an Olympic silver medal.

question: At the 2020 Tokyo Olympics (held in 2021), Neeraj Chopra won India's first-ever Olympic gold medal in Athletics, in which event, with a throw of 87.58m?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Javelin Throw.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, Neeraj Chopra won India's first-ever Olympic gold medal in Athletics, in the Javelin Throw event, with a throw of 87.58m.

 

• This made him only the second Indian to win an individual Olympic gold, after Abhinav Bindra (2008).

 

• India won a total of 7 medals (1 Gold + 2 Silver + 4 Bronze) at Tokyo 2020, ranking 48th, with other medallists including Mirabai Chanu (Silver, Weightlifting), Ravi Kumar Dahiya (Silver, Wrestling), P.V. Sindhu (Bronze, Badminton), Lovlina Borgohain (Bronze, Boxing), Bajrang Punia (Bronze, Wrestling), and the Men's Hockey Team (Bronze).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tokyo 2020 was also notable as the first Olympics to be delayed (due to COVID-19), and as the first Asian city to host the Summer Olympics twice (Tokyo had also hosted in 1964).

 

NOTE

 

• Discus Throw, Shot Put and Hammer Throw (Options 1, 3, 4) are all athletics field events, but Neeraj Chopra's specific historic gold-medal-winning event was the Javelin Throw.

question: At the 2024 Paris Olympics, Manu Bhaker achieved which historic 'first' for Indian women, winning two bronze medals in a single edition?
option_1: First Indian woman to win an Olympic gold medal
option_2: First Indian woman to win two medals in a single Olympic edition since independence
option_3: First Indian woman to compete in Olympic shooting
option_4: First Indian woman fencer to qualify for the Olympics
solution_text:
The correct answer is First Indian woman to win two medals in a single Olympic edition since independence.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the 2024 Paris Olympics, Manu Bhaker won two Bronze medals — in the Women's 10m Air Pistol (individual) and the Mixed 10m Air Pistol Team event (with Sarabjot Singh) — becoming the first Indian woman to win two medals in a single Olympic edition since independence, and also the first Indian woman to win an Olympic shooting medal.

 

• Other Indian medallists at Paris 2024 included Neeraj Chopra (Silver, Javelin Throw), Swapnil Kusale (Bronze, Men's 50m Rifle 3 Positions), the Indian Men's Hockey Team (Bronze), and Aman Sehrawat (Bronze, Wrestling) — India's youngest-ever individual Olympic medallist, at age 21.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhavani Devi, though not a medallist at these Games, made history separately as the first Indian fencer to qualify for the Olympic Games, while Vinesh Phogat reached the wrestling final but was controversially disqualified for being 100g overweight.

 

NOTE

 

• First Olympic gold, first shooting competitor, and first fencer to qualify (Options 1, 3, 4) describe other athletes or inaccurate claims; Manu Bhaker's specific 2024 'first' is winning two medals in a single Olympic edition.

question: Which Indian wrestler became India's youngest-ever individual Olympic medal winner, at age 21, by winning a bronze medal in the Men's Freestyle 57kg category at the 2024 Paris Olympics?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aman Sehrawat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aman Sehrawat, by winning a Bronze medal in Men's Freestyle Wrestling 57kg at the 2024 Paris Olympics, became India's youngest-ever individual Olympic medal winner, at age 21.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• This 2024 achievement adds to the list of notable Indian wrestling Olympic medallists, alongside K.D. Jadhav (1952), Sushil Kumar (2008, 2012), Yogeshwar Dutt (2012), Sakshi Malik (2016), Bajrang Punia and Ravi Kumar Dahiya (2020).

 

NOTE

 

• Bajrang Punia, Ravi Kumar Dahiya and Yogeshwar Dutt (Options 1, 2, 4) are all accomplished Indian Olympic wrestling medallists, but the specific 'youngest-ever individual medallist' distinction (2024) belongs to Aman Sehrawat.

question: The Olympic motto, 'Citius, Altius, Fortius', translates to which of the following in English?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Faster, Higher, Stronger.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Olympic Motto, 'Citius - Altius - Fortius', translates to 'Faster, Higher, Stronger'.

 

• The Olympic Rings' colours (Blue, Yellow, Black, Green, Red) represent Europe, Asia, Africa, Australia, and America respectively.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The International Olympic Committee (IOC) was founded in 1894 by Pierre de Coubertin, and is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland, with Kirsty Coventry as its current president.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Peace, Unity, Sport', 'Stronger, Together, Forever', and 'Higher, Faster, United' (Options 1, 3, 4) are not the correct translation of the Olympic Motto, which is specifically 'Faster, Higher, Stronger'.

question: Which of the following statements about the modern Olympic Games' history is correct?
option_1: The first Summer Olympics were held in 1896 at Athens, Greece, and the first Winter Olympics were held in 1924 at Chamonix, France
option_2: The first Summer Olympics were held in Paris in 1900, and Winter Olympics began in 1930
option_3: The Olympics have never been cancelled in their modern history
option_4: The first Winter Olympics were held before the first Summer Olympics
solution_text:
The correct answer is The first Summer Olympics were held in 1896 at Athens, Greece, and the first Winter Olympics were held in 1924 at Chamonix, France.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first Summer Olympics were held in 1896, at Athens, Greece; the first Winter Olympics were held in 1924, at Chamonix, France.

 

• The Olympics were cancelled three times due to wars: 1916, 1940, and 1944. The Olympics are organised every 4 years, and Olympic Day is observed on 23 June.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cities that have hosted the Summer Olympics three times are London, Paris, and Los Angeles, with the USA having hosted the Olympics most often (8 times).

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 all misstate historical facts; the Olympics have in fact been cancelled three times (1916, 1940, 1944), the first Summer Olympics predate the first Winter Olympics, and the correct years/venues are specifically 1896 Athens (Summer) and 1924 Chamonix (Winter).

question: The 2024 Paris Olympics marked Paris hosting the Summer Olympics for the third time. In which two earlier years did Paris also host the Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1900 and 1924.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Paris hosted the Summer Olympics for the 3rd time in 2024, having also hosted in 1900 and 1924.

 

• At the 2024 Paris Olympics (33rd edition), the torchbearer was Abhinav Bindra, with the theme 'Games Wide Open'; India's opening flag bearers were P.V. Sindhu and Achanta Sharath Kamal, and closing flag bearers were Manu Bhaker and P.R. Sreejesh. India ranked 71st, winning 6 medals (1 Silver + 5 Bronze).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Coincidentally, India's first-ever Olympic participation also took place in Paris, in 1900 — the very same year that Paris first hosted the Games, creating a symbolic historical link across 124 years to the 2024 Paris Olympics.

 

NOTE

 

• 1896/1908, 1912/1936 and 1920/1948 (Options 1, 3, 4) do not match Paris's actual hosting years; the correct earlier years are specifically 1900 and 1924.

question: Which of the following correctly describes the composition of an Olympic gold medal, as documented in the notes?
option_1: It is made entirely of pure gold
option_2: It is made up of silver (92.5 to 95%) with a plating of pure gold, which must contain at least 6 grams of pure gold
option_3: It is made entirely of bronze with a gold coating
option_4: It contains no silver at all, only gold and copper alloy
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is made up of silver (92.5 to 95%) with a plating of pure gold, which must contain at least 6 grams of pure gold.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An Olympic gold medal is made up of silver (92.5% to 95%), finished with a plating of pure gold, which must contain at least 6 grams of pure gold.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• This fact is often surprising to the general public, as popular perception assumes Olympic gold medals are made entirely of solid gold, when in reality they are predominantly silver with only a thin gold plating meeting a minimum weight requirement.

 

NOTE

 

• Pure gold, bronze with gold coating, and gold-copper alloy without silver (Options 1, 3, 4) all misstate the actual documented composition; an Olympic gold medal is specifically silver-based with a minimum 6g pure gold plating.

question: The Summer Youth Olympics, held for athletes aged 15 to 18 years, had its first edition in 2010 in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Singapore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Summer Youth Olympics, governed by the IOC, held every 4 years for athletes aged 15-18, had its 1st edition in 2010, in Singapore.

 

• Jeremy Lalrinnunga marked India's inaugural gold medal moment at the Youth Olympics, at the 2018 Summer Youth Olympics (Buenos Aires, Argentina).

 

• The 4th edition, in 2026, will be held in Dakar, Senegal — marking the first Olympic event held in Africa.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2026 Dakar Youth Olympics will be a landmark moment for the Olympic movement, as it will represent the first time any Olympic-branded event (Summer, Winter, or Youth) has been hosted on the African continent.

 

NOTE

 

• Nanjing, Buenos Aires and Dakar (Options 1, 2, 4) are all hosts of various Youth Olympics editions (2014, 2018, and the upcoming 2026 respectively), but the very first edition (2010) was specifically held in Singapore.

question: Which Indian athlete became the first Indian woman to participate in the Winter Olympics, representing India in Alpine Skiing at the 1988 Calgary Winter Olympics?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shailaja Kumar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Shailaja Kumar became the first Indian woman to participate in the Winter Olympics, representing India in the 'Alpine Skiing' event at the 1988 Calgary Winter Olympics.

 

• India's first Winter Olympics participation overall was in 1964, at Innsbruck, Austria, where Jeremy Bujakowski participated in the men's downhill event in alpine skiing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Arif Khan represented India in Skiing at the 2022 Beijing Winter Olympics, the most recent Winter Olympics edition documented, with 2026 (Italy) being the next upcoming edition.

 

NOTE

 

• Jeremy Bujakowski, Aditi Ashoka and Arif Khan (Options 2, 3, 4) are documented in other contexts (India's first Winter Olympics participant, Olympic golf, and the most recent Winter Olympics skier respectively), not as the first Indian woman at the Winter Olympics.

question: Murlikant Petkar won a Gold medal in the Men's 50m Freestyle (swimming) at the 1972 Paralympics, becoming India's first Paralympic medallist. Where were the first-ever Paralympic Games held, in 1960?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rome, Italy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first Paralympic Games were held in 1960, in Rome, Italy, organised by the International Paralympics Committee (IPC), headquartered in Bonn, Germany.

 

• India's first Paralympic participation was in 1968, at Tel Aviv, Israel. Murlikant Petkar won a Gold medal in the Men's 50m Freestyle, becoming India's first Paralympic medallist, in 1972.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's Paralympic movement saw further landmark moments with Deepa Malik, the first female Paralympic medallist (Silver, Shot Put, 2016), and Avani Lekhara, the first female Paralympic gold medallist (2020).

 

NOTE

 

• Tokyo, Tel Aviv and Bonn (Options 1, 3, 4) are associated with other Paralympic milestones (a future Olympic host, India's first participation venue, and the IPC's headquarters respectively), not the first-ever Paralympic Games, which were held in Rome in 1960.

question: At the 2024 Paris Paralympics, India achieved its best-ever rank (18th), winning a total of 29 medals. Which young Indian archer became India's youngest Paralympic medal winner and the world's first international female archer to compete using her feet?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sheetal Devi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the 2024 Paris Paralympics, 17-year-old Sheetal Devi (along with Rakesh Kumar) won a Bronze medal in the archery mixed team compound open event, becoming India's youngest Paralympic medal winner.

 

• She is also the world's first international female archer to compete in archery using her feet.

 

• India won a total of 29 medals (7 Gold, 9 Silver, 13 Bronze) at these Games, achieving its best-ever rank of 18th.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Among the gold medal winners at the 2024 Paris Paralympics were Avani Lekhara (Shooting), Nitesh Kumar (Badminton), Sumit Antil (Javelin Throw), Harvinder Singh (Archery), Dharambir Nain (Club Throw), Praveen Kumar (High Jump), and Navdeep Singh (Javelin Throw).

 

NOTE

 

• Avani Lekhara, Deepa Malik and Bhagyashree Jadhav (Options 1, 3, 4) are all significant Indian Paralympians, but the specific 'youngest medallist and feet-archery pioneer' distinctions belong to Sheetal Devi.

question: The Commonwealth Games, first held in 1930 at Hamilton, Canada, were originally known by which name?
solution_text:
The correct answer is British Empire Games.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Commonwealth Games, first held in 1930, in Hamilton, Canada, were originally known as the 'British Empire Games', with approximately 400 athletes from 11 countries participating in these inaugural Games.

 

• India's debut was in 1934, in London (as British India); Rashid Anwar won India's first medal, in wrestling, in 1934; Milkha Singh won India's first gold medal, in 1958.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India hosted the Commonwealth Games in 2010, in New Delhi, achieving its best-ever performance, ranking 2nd with 101 medals (38 Gold + 27 Silver + 36 Bronze) — where Geeta Phogat became the first Indian woman wrestler to win gold.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Empire Games of Nations', 'Commonwealth Sporting Union Games', and 'Imperial Athletic Championship' (Options 1, 3, 4) are not the original historical name of the Commonwealth Games; that is specifically the 'British Empire Games'.

question: At the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham (UK), India's latest edition performance, which Indian athlete won India's first-ever gold medal in athletics at these Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eldhose Paul.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the 2022 Commonwealth Games, Birmingham (UK), Eldhose Paul won India's first gold medal in athletics at these Games.

 

• India finished with a total of 61 medals (22 Gold + 16 Silver + 23 Bronze), ranking 4th, with wrestling contributing 12 medals (6 Gold + 1 Silver + 5 Bronze). Mirabai Chanu won gold in weightlifting, Sanket Sagar was the first Indian athlete to win a medal, and Avinash Sable won a silver medal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The David Dixon Award, presented to the outstanding athlete of each Commonwealth Games edition, and Karnam Malleswari's distinction as the first female Commonwealth Games medallist (Bronze, 1994), are other notable Commonwealth Games facts documented in the notes.

 

NOTE

 

• Avinash Sable, Sanket Sagar and Mirabai Chanu (Options 1, 2, 4) are all significant 2022 Commonwealth Games medallists, but the specific 'first gold medal in athletics' distinction at these Games belongs to Eldhose Paul.

question: The Asian Games (Asiad), held every 4 years, had their first edition in 1951, hosted by which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Delhi, India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first Asian Games were held in 1951, in New Delhi, India. At this edition, Japan ranked 1st, while India ranked 2nd, winning 51 medals (15 Gold).

 

• Lavy Pinto won India's first gold medal in athletics (100m sprint) at these Games; Sachin Nag was the first player to win a gold medal overall.

 

• India has hosted the Asian Games twice: 1951 and 1982.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 19th Asian Games (2022) were held in Hangzhou, China; the upcoming 20th Asian Games (2026) will be held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan — showing the Games' continued rotation primarily among East and South Asian host nations.

 

NOTE

 

• Tokyo, Jakarta and Beijing (Options 1, 3, 4) have all hosted various editions of the Asian Games over the decades, but the very first edition, in 1951, was specifically hosted by New Delhi, India.

question: At the 19th Asian Games (2022, Hangzhou, China), held from 23 September to 8 October 2023 (postponed due to the pandemic), India achieved which historic medal tally, ranking 4th?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 107 Medals (28 Gold + 38 Silver + 41 Bronze).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the 19th Asian Games (Hangzhou, China), held 23 September - 8 October 2023 (postponed from 2022 due to the pandemic), India won a total of 107 medals (28 Gold + 38 Silver + 41 Bronze), ranking 4th.

 

• Palak Gulia won the gold medal in the women's 10m air pistol at these Games.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• This 107-medal tally represented a historic milestone for India, marking the first time India crossed the 100-medal mark at a single edition of the Asian Games.

 

NOTE

 

• 51 medals/15 Gold, 61 medals/22 Gold, and 29 medals topped by India (Options 1, 2, 4) correspond to the 1951 Asian Games, the 2022 Commonwealth Games, and India's 2017 Asian Athletics Championship performance respectively, not the 19th Asian Games (2022/2023).

question: Which of the following governing body-and-founding-year pairs is correctly matched, based on the sports institutions documented?
solution_text:
The correct answer is ICC (International Cricket Council) - 1909.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The ICC (International Cricket Council) was formed in 1909, headquartered in Dubai, UAE; BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India) was formed in 1928, headquartered in Mumbai.

 

• FIFA was founded in 1904 (not 1930, which is instead the year of the first FIFA World Cup, hosted and won by Uruguay); the FIH (International Hockey Federation) was founded in 1924 (not 1937, which is instead the year the All India Football Federation was formed).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cricket is traditionally referred to as the 'Game of Gentlemen', and its formats are structured as Test (450 overs/5 days), ODI (50 overs/1 day), and T20 (20 overs).

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 each misstate the founding year of a sports governing body; only ICC-1909 (Option 1) is correctly matched among the given options.
